amanda: noticing a spike in p95/p99 for /v1/generate since last night. customer reports latency regressions on long-chat sessions. p95 went 210ms -> 480ms, p99 520ms -> 1.4s. any obvious recent changes?
amanda: repro is on dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-ded-3', model llama-2-13b-q4f; seq length ~1500 tokens.
raj: we rolled kernel optimizer (FlashAttn2 + SDPA selector) in runtime 0.21.3 yesterday, had a canary then full rollout at 03:10 UTC.
raj: deploy-bot shows canary 0.21.3 -> promoted at 03:09:45 by pipeline. :sweat:
deploy-bot: canary promoted: runtime/0.21.3 -> all clusters (pipeline #4728)
sophie: any APM traces?
amanda: pasted sample trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/abcd1234 (internal) — shows a long stall in kernel-selection/compile step then repeated SDPA fallback.
raj: that matches a suspicion: kernel selector is preferring flash_attn2 for certain shapes then falling back to a slow SDPA path due to an internal check failing (padding alignment). fallback adds ~300-700ms on hot path.
mike: do we have flamegraphs?
amanda: grabbed a perf snapshot: top function is `choose_attention_kernel` and we see many `launch_sdpa_kernel` calls.
amanda: snippet from node logs:
```
I0427 03:12:09 kernel_selector.cc:214] model=llama-2-13b seq=1536 batch=1 -> selected=flash_attn2
W0427 03:12:09 kernel_selector.cc:332] flash_attn2 not applicable (alignment=7) -> falling back to sdpa
E0427 03:12:10 runtime_perf.cc:87] kernel_launch_latency_ms=412
```
raj: thanks. I already have a local repro. i can reproduce with our bench script:
```
python bench.py --model llama-2-13b-q4f --seq 1536 --batch 1 --kernel-selector=auto
```
raj: when I force `--kernel-selector=flash_attn` I see many kernel failures, forcing `--kernel-selector=sdpa` restores previous timings (~200ms p95).
sophie: immediate mitigations?
raj: options: 1) roll back 0.21.3 to 0.21.2 on affected pools (fast, low risk) 2) flip runtime flag to disable flash_attn globally: `ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0` (hot config) 3) add a targeted policy to route long seq requests to fallback pool (policy routing) 4) patch kernel selector to prefer sdpa for shapes where flash fails (requires a build).
mike: for customer impact, should we do 1+2 now?
amanda: I'd prefer hot config flip first to stop new tail latencies, then rollback if needed. flip is immediate and reversible.
raj: I agree. I can push hot config: `PATCH /internal/config/runtime` with body `{\n  "ENABLE_FLASHATTN": "0"\n}` and reload agent.
raj: performing patch now...
infra-bot: config change detected for runtime: key=ENABLE_FLASHATTN old=1 new=0 by raj (at 2410123480)
raj: agent reload returned OK.
amanda: re-running the bench now...
raj: can you test both 1536 and 2048 sequences?
amanda: results: seq=1536 p95=220ms, seq=2048 p95=230ms, p99s are ~480ms — close to baseline.
mike: good. customer reported improvement?
amanda: customer SLA page shows reduced errors, they confirm latency is back to acceptable levels. :thumbsup:
sophie: next steps: root cause = selector allowed flash_attn path for misaligned shapes; fallback path is expensive. Need fix in kernel selection heuristics + add unit tests for alignment checks. Also add runtime config to allow selective per-model toggles.
raj: I'll open an infra PR to tighten selector: ensure alignment % 16 == 0 check and avoid runtime fallback for these shapes; will add a guarded compile flag `-DENABLE_FLASHATTN=1` default off in canary until tests pass.
raj: owning bisect/PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5581
sophie: I'll update runbook and create incident ticket INC-1234 (support) with timeline and customer callbacks.
mike: also add monitoring alert: if p95 jumps >2x vs baseline for 5m on any dedicated pool trigger P1 page.
amanda: assigning follow-ups:
- raj: kernel selector patch + PR (target: 2d)
- sophie: incident doc + customer comms (today)
- mike: alert rule + fallback routing policy (today)
- amanda: validate canary when kernel fix merged

amanda: repro steps for SRE/Support to validate locally: 
1) checkout commit: `git checkout release/0.21.x`
2) run bench: `python bench.py --model llama-2-13b-q4f --seq 1536 --batch 1`
3) toggle flag: `export ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0` or call internal config patch endpoint (see above)
4) curl sample request: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b-q4f","input":"x" ,"max_tokens":1600}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate
```
5) check `/metrics` for `runtime_attention_kernel_choice{kernel="sdpa"}` counters and verify p95 on grafana panel `runtime.p95.latency`

raj: note: longer-term we should add a kernel compatibility matrix per (model, quant, seq, hw) to avoid selector surprises.
sophie: thanks team. i'll post an incident summary to #incidents and loop in account team for customer update.
mike: great work. leaving this thread open until PR lands and rollback fully validated.
amanda: closing the immediate P1 — latency mitigated by hot-config flip. will reopen if we see regression.
infra-bot: incident INC-1234 created by sophie (severity=P1)
